name: IPv6 Subnet Calculator
description: Calculate IPv6 subnet capacity, prefix relationships and subnet counts from IPv6 prefix lengths.
search_intent: Calculate IPv6 subnet sizes and determine how many smaller subnets fit inside a larger IPv6 prefix.
calculation: Subnet bits = subnet prefix - parent prefix. Number of subnets = 2^subnetBits. Host/interface bits = 128 - subnet prefix. Addresses per subnet = 2^hostBits. Require integer prefixes from 0 through 128 and subnet prefix >= parent prefix. Use BigInt/string-safe output where ordinary JavaScript numbers cannot represent the exact integer.
limitations: IPv6 does not use IPv4-style broadcast addresses.
The mathematical address count should not be interpreted as a recommendation to assign every address.
A /64 is conventional for many IPv6 LAN use cases, but network design depends on the deployment.
